Article Submission Abstract
This article examines the loan translation strategy of English terminology in Kiswahili and its effects by focusing on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through selected entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The main aim of this investigation is to assess the contribution of the loan translation of English vocabulary to the overall development of the Kiswahili language. According to this article, this area has not been prioritized among the various translation topics that have already been studied. This has motivated the researcher to address this area. The data for this article was collected in the field from departments and institutions located in the city of Dar es Salaam through interviews, questionnaires, and library-based data sources. The departments and institutions involved in data collection are: the Department of Foreign Languages and Linguistics, TATAKI from the University of Dar es Salaam, as well as BAKIZA. These departments and institutions are located in Ubungo District, Dar es Salaam Region, where the researcher was able to conduct inquiries and hold face-to-face interviews with translation experts. In addition, data was collected from various texts from the library data source. For instance, dictionaries, dissertations, journals, and several books were used, depending on the subject of this article. The objectives of the article have been achieved by being guided by the Theory of Scientific Terminology pioneered by Kiingi (1989) and further developed by Kiingi (1992) and Kiingi (1998), as well as Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001). Likewise, the data for this article was analyzed using a descriptive approach. In addition, the findings have shown that Kiswahili has acquired numerous terminologies in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through the loan translation strategy. This article is important for linguists as it identifies various English-language terminologies in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry that have been incorporated into Kiswahili through loan translation. Introduction  
Translation is the act of transferring a message contained in writing from the source language to the target language without altering the intended meaning in the source language. Thus, translation is regarded as a method of learning foreign languages, showcasing various cultures, and transmitting the knowledge and skills of other communities, such as information on scientific and technological advancements. The motivation that drives a person to translate the message from the source language to the target language is the desire to facilitate communication among speakers of different languages. We can therefore say that translation is a means or even a bridge to bring together various communities that speak different languages. Moreover, loan translation is one method of coining new vocabulary, where a concept from the source language is adopted and translated into the target language; for example, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, and so on. The strategy of borrowing through loan translation has gained momentum due to the significant developments occurring in the field of science and technology, coupled with society’s advancement into modernity, resulting in a high demand for vocabulary to describe various concepts. The researcher of this article investigates the loan translation strategy of English vocabulary into Kiswahili. The researcher has focused on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through selected entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The main objective is to evaluate the contribution of loan translation of English vocabulary to the overall development of the Kiswahili language. Translation work has been carried out numerous times around the world (Mwansoko, 1996; Malangwa, 2005; Giambruno, 2008; Baker & Saldanha, 2008; Malangwa, 2010; Malangwa, 2014). Crystal (2002) explains that new technology often has an impact on language, whether written or spoken. This is the reason why the English language has influenced Swahili at the lexical level. Furthermore, Crystal (2004) observes that the greatest influence on the lexical development of Swahili has come from English, which is the main language of Information and Communication Technology, as well as from Arabic. Mwaro-Were (2000), along with Adika and Kevogo (2014), explain that since ancient times, lexical borrowing has had a significant influence on the Swahili language. Lexicologically, several foreign languages have influenced Swahili to varying degrees. Some of these languages are Portuguese, Persian, Arabic, Hindi, German, and English. This clearly demonstrates that advancements in science and technology have had a significant impact on the Swahili language. Translation plays a role in promoting and spreading a language, especially through the process of transferring structural expressions from the source language to the target language. Additionally, translation brings satisfaction to the translator when they successfully complete their work effectively (Mwansoko, 2016). Nassor (2017), for his part, explains that the rate of coining Swahili terminology has increased significantly in recent years compared to the 1960s. He further adds that at the end of the 19th century, the Swahili community experienced major advancements in science and technology, as well as in other fields. As a result, the Swahili language has undergone significant changes. Therefore, efforts to develop Swahili terminologically intensified in order to keep pace with these advancements. Alongside studies that examine the development of the Swahili language due to advancements in science and technology, this article also addresses this issue but focuses specifically on the field of loan translation in the areas of biology, physics, and chemistry. Adolph (2019), on his part, investigated terminology in the fields of medicine and computers, originating from English in Swahili and the processes of their adaptation. His research findings clearly demonstrate that Swahili has expanded its vocabulary through the adaptation of medical and computer-related terms from English. Consequently, this adaptation has contributed to the growth of Swahili due to the significant expansion of scientific and technological vocabulary in the areas of computers and medicine. Language grows and changes every day according to the development of society. One of the main criteria for the growth and change of a language is the increase in terminology. According to Adolph (2019), in order for terminologies to increase in a language, new terms must be created. Terms are formed in a language so that its culture can accommodate concepts that were previously not part of that culture. This note is very important in this article as it shows how language grows and meets the communication needs among community members. This article examines the strategy of loan translation of English terminology into Swahili and its effects by focusing on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry, in contrast to Adolph's (2019) study, which investigates the development of the Swahili language through the adaptation of medical and computer terminology. Many scholars who have addressed borrowing agree that borrowing is the transfer of lexical elements from one language to another (Haugen, 1950; Polomé, 1980; Adolph, 2014; Winford, 2003). This article is divided into five sections: The first section is the introduction, in which the general concept of translation and its functions are explained, together with the concept of loan translation. The second section explains the theory that guided the analysis of the data in this article. The third section describes the methodology. The fourth section analyzes data on the strategy of loan translation from English into Swahili and its effects. The discussion concerns terminology in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The fifth section is the conclusion. Theory  
The Theory of Scientific Terminology was used to provide data for this article. The Theory of Scientific Terminology is associated with Kiingi (1989), who is the original founder of this theory. Later, this theory was further developed by Kiingi (1992, 1998); Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001); Kevogo, Mukuthuria, and Ontieri (2018); and Kevogo (2020). This theory contains scientific criteria for effective terminology, which play a central role in the evaluation conducted in our article. Several scholars, such as Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008), have clearly outlined various principles that should be followed during the borrowing, adaptation, and formation of terminology from indigenous and foreign languages into Swahili. These principles are elaborated in Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008). This involves creating terminology using Swahili, Bantu languages, other African languages, and foreign languages. In addition to many other views expressed by Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (1997) regarding these principles, they recommend the following guidelines: Terminology should reflect the distinctive features of the concepts they represent (or at least suggest such features) and be clear to the intended users. If terminology is formed using compounding and word combination techniques, the following aspects must be considered:
The number of words combined or joined should not exceed two. Hyphens should not be used to separate compound terms, because in Swahili such terms are usually pronounced as a single word, with the primary stress on only one syllable. For example: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") and -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Such terms should not have more than four syllables, since Swahili words usually have an average of between one and five syllables. Terminology must be highly derivable in order to generate other related terms within the relevant domain or field. This will allow terms representing closely related or derivationally connected concepts to logically reflect that connection. For example: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), and -siyo wa taifa ("un-national"). Terminology (especially those with overlapping shades of meaning) must maintain consistency in sequence. The following terms, for example, demonstrate an acceptable alignment of sequence: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, and so on. Terminology must be adequate, meaning it should reflect the characteristics of the concepts they represent (and not, for instance, contradict them). For example, the term “tahakiki ya maandishi” is inappropriate because it generally refers to the evaluation of writing at large, rather than the analysis or critique of literature. Terminology must also be short and understandable. Lengthy terms, such as “majira ya majani kupukutika” (when the dry season approaches), are unsuitable because they do not adhere to the principle of linguistic economy. These principles are essential in terminology creation as they provide guidance on what should be done regarding borrowing, formation, and adaptation. In addition, methods for creating terminology have been proposed. Let us look at these methods below: first, translation, especially from languages known to be international, such as English, French, Spanish, and so on. Second, forming terminology based on conceptual frameworks. This theory is relevant as it provides the foundations to follow during the translation process. Likewise, it clarifies the methods of terminology creation. 

Methodology  
Every researcher uses appropriate and clear methods for their research. This article is the result of a descriptive research conducted both in the library and in the field. The researcher collected data from the Department of Foreign Languages and Linguistics, TATAKI from the University of Dar es Salaam, as well as BAKIZA in Ubungo District, Dar es Salaam Region, where data was gathered using interviews, questionnaires, and a library data source. According to Krishnaswami and Ranganatham (2005), interviews are a data collection method that involves an exchange between the researcher and the respondent with the aim of obtaining information related to the topic under investigation. Using the interview method, the researcher was able to conduct face-to-face interviews with translation experts from the aforementioned departments and institutions. A questionnaire is prepared with the aim of collecting important information from respondents (Mugenda and Mugenda, 2003). The questionnaire method can be conducted either face-to-face or through non-face-to-face means, depending on advancements in science and technology. Advancements in science and technology have facilitated the sending of various questionnaires by researchers to their respondents electronically (via web and email). However, the researcher of this article used face-to-face questionnaires because the informants were in the same location and easily accessible. In addition, the researcher reviewed various writings such as journals, dissertations, dictionaries, and so on from the library data source. Research Findings

The findings of this article were obtained after an investigation and analysis of data concerning the development of Swahili through the loan translation of terminology from English. Loan translation is a strategy for term creation involving word-for-word transfer of both structural elements and general concepts. The structure of terms created using the loan translation strategy changes to conform to the morphological and phonological rules of the target language. From the methods of interviews, questionnaires, and the library data source, it was found that several terms in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry—through the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012)—have been incorporated into Swahili from English via the loan translation strategy. The following examples support this statement:

The findings of this article indicate that terminology in biology, chemistry, and physics has been translated through the strategy of loan translation from English into Swahili. This is due to the high demand for these terms among Swahili users, as well as the development and growth of science and technology. This situation compels Swahili to use the loan translation strategy in order to meet the communication needs of Swahili speakers and to incorporate concepts derived from these terms. Benefits for Language Translators and Global Recognition of TUKI

The strategy of borrowing English terms into Swahili through loan translation as a method for creating Swahili terminology has played a significant role in providing opportunities for language translators. For instance, TUKI (2012) has translated an adequate vocabulary related to the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry by employing the loan translation strategy and other forms of borrowing; however, this article focuses on the loan translation strategy. This institution has translated vocabulary from biology, physics, and chemistry from English into Swahili. Indeed, this work has brought global recognition to TUKI due to its great importance in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. Alongside international recognition, those involved in this work have also benefited economically from sales made through published books, including the standardized Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary. This is attributed to the significance of its contents, the care taken in its preparation, and especially the expertise and professionalism of the dictionary’s compilers. This clearly demonstrates that its users have great confidence in this dictionary and are therefore willing to make purchases without hesitation. The Global Spread of the Swahili Language

Based on information from respondents (field data) as well as library data, the researcher has found that the loan translation strategy implemented by TUKI (2012) has contributed to the worldwide recognition of Swahili, since the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry are used globally due to advancements in science and technology, as well as their importance to students studying these subjects and to Swahili speakers in general. Furthermore, speakers of other languages apart from Swahili need to learn the vocabulary of these fields in the Swahili language. This situation leads them to acquire several Swahili language books, including this dictionary. All these factors have significantly contributed to the overall spread of Swahili throughout the world. The global spread of Swahili has encouraged people from various countries to learn Swahili, appreciate it, and value it highly.

Conclusion

The analysis in this article confirms the argument that the loan translation strategy has been used as one of the methods for borrowing English terminology into Swahili. The terms examined in this article are those from the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. In the case of biology, terms such as: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, biennial plants, nitrogen, occiput, spermatid, and zoology were identified. The researcher also considered the loan translation strategy in the field of chemistry. The following are some of the terms addressed in this field: absolute, acetate, active mass, masi tendaji, acylation, bond energy, pesticide, x-radiation, and zymology. Additionally, the researcher of this article has also examined the effects of the loan translation strategy on the Swahili language, language translators, students of biology, physics, and chemistry, speakers of other languages learning Swahili, and Swahili speakers in general. The findings of this article have revealed that this strategy has been beneficial to language translators, especially those translating from English into Swahili. A good example is the experts at TUKI who translated terms from these fields from English into Swahili. These translators have improved economically due to the global sale of this dictionary. It has also become evident that TUKI, which is now known as TATAKI, has become recognized and established worldwide. Alongside this, this strategy has also contributed to the global spread of Swahili. This and this work are an attraction to Swahili speakers, speakers of other languages learning Swahili, and other people. The researcher of this article suggests that other borrowing strategies such as naturalization and adaptation should be studied. In addition, other fields such as computers and medicine should be addressed in the same way that the researcher of this article addressed the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. Muhtasari wa Uwasilishaji wa Makala
Makala hii inachunguza mkakati wa ukalimani wa msamiati wa Kiingereza katika Kiswahili na athari zake kwa kuzingatia nyanja za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia kupitia viingilio vilivyoteuliwa kutoka kwenye Kamusi ya Baiolojia, Fizikia, na Kemia (2012). Lengo kuu la uchunguzi huu ni kutathmini mchango wa ukalimani wa msamiati wa Kiingereza katika maendeleo ya jumla ya lugha ya Kiswahili. Kulingana na makala hii, eneo hili halijapewa kipaumbele kati ya mada mbalimbali za tafsiri ambazo tayari zimeshachunguzwa. Hii imemhamasisha mtafiti kulishughulikia eneo hili. Taarifa za makala hii zilikusanywa kwenye maeneo ya kazi kutoka idara na taasisi zilizopo katika jiji la Dar es Salaam kupitia mahojiano, dodoso, na vyanzo vya taarifa za maktaba. Idara na taasisi zilizohusika katika ukusanyaji wa data ni: Idara ya Lugha za Kigeni na Isimu, TATAKI kutoka Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam, pamoja na BAKIZA. Idara na taasisi hizi ziko katika Wilaya ya Ubungo, Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, ambako mtafiti aliweza kufanya utafiti na kufanya mahojiano ya ana kwa ana na wataalamu wa tafsiri. Zaidi ya hayo, data ilikusanywa kutoka kwa maandishi mbalimbali kutoka chanzo cha data cha maktaba. Kwa mfano, kamusi, tasnifu, majarida, na vitabu kadhaa vilitumika, kulingana na mada ya makala haya. Malengo ya makala yametimia kwa kuongozwa na Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi iliyoasisiwa na Kiingi (1989) na kuendelezwa zaidi na Kiingi (1992) na Kiingi (1998), pamoja na Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001). Vilevile, data ya makala hii ilichanganuliwa kwa kutumia mbinu elezi. Aidha, matokeo yameonyesha kwamba Kiswahili kimepata istilahi nyingi katika nyanja za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia kupitia mkakati wa uhawilishaji wa maneno. Makala hii ni muhimu kwa wanaisimu kwa kuwa inatambua istilahi mbalimbali za lugha ya Kiingereza katika nyanja za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia ambazo zimeingizwa katika Kiswahili kupitia uhawilishaji wa maneno. Inashauriwa kwamba watafiti wa lugha wachunguze mbinu nyingine za kukopa ambazo zinakuza Kiswahili, kama vile urekebishaji na uasili. La hapana. Utangulizi  
Tafsiri ni kitendo cha kuhamisha ujumbe uliomo katika maandishi kutoka lugha chanzi kwenda lugha lengwa bila kubadili maana iliyokusudiwa katika lugha chanzi. Hivyo basi, tafsiri huchukuliwa kama mbinu ya kujifunza lugha za kigeni, kuonyesha tamaduni mbalimbali, na kuhamisha maarifa na stadi za jamii nyingine, kama vile taarifa kuhusu maendeleo ya kisayansi na kiteknolojia. Msukumo unaomfanya mtu kutafsiri ujumbe kutoka lugha chanzi kwenda lugha lengwa ni hamu ya kufanikisha mawasiliano kati ya wazungumzaji wa lugha tofauti. Kwa hiyo, tunaweza kusema kuwa tafsiri ni njia au hata daraja la kuunganisha jamii mbalimbali zinazozungumza lugha tofauti. Aidha, tafsiri ya mkopo ni mbinu mojawapo ya kuunda msamiati mpya, ambapo dhana kutoka lugha chanzi inachukuliwa na kutafsiriwa katika lugha lengwa; kwa mfano, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, na kadhalika. Mkakati wa kukopa kupitia tafsiri ya mkopo umeongezeka kasi kutokana na maendeleo makubwa yanayotokea katika uwanja wa sayansi na teknolojia, pamoja na maendeleo ya jamii kuingia katika ukisasa, na hivyo kusababisha kuhitajika kwa msamiati mwingi wa kuelezea dhana mbalimbali. Mtafiti wa makala hii anachunguza mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo ya msamiati wa Kiingereza katika Kiswahili. Mtafiti amejikita kwenye nyanja za biolojia, fizikia, na kemia kupitia maandiko yaliyoteuliwa kutoka kwenye Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia, na Kemia (2012). Lengo kuu ni kutathmini mchango wa uhawilisho wa mkopo wa msamiati wa Kiingereza katika maendeleo ya jumla ya lugha ya Kiswahili. Kazi ya tafsiri imefanyika mara nyingi duniani kote (Mwansoko, 1996; Malangwa, 2005; Giambruno, 2008; Baker & Saldanha, 2008; Malangwa, 2010; Malangwa, 2014). Crystal (2002) anaeleza kwamba teknolojia mpya mara nyingi inaathiri lugha, iwe ya maandishi au ya mazungumzo. Hii ndiyo sababu lugha ya Kiingereza imeathiri Kiswahili katika ngazi ya msamiati. Zaidi ya hayo, Crystal (2004) anabainisha kwamba ushawishi mkubwa zaidi katika maendeleo ya msamiati wa Kiswahili umetokana na Kiingereza, ambacho ndicho lugha kuu ya Teknolojia ya Habari na Mawasiliano, na pia kutoka kwa Kiarabu. Mwaro-Were (2000), pamoja na Adika na Kevogo (2014), wanaeleza kuwa tangu nyakati za kale, ukopeshaji wa msamiati umeathiri kwa kiasi kikubwa lugha ya Kiswahili. Kileksikoni, lugha nyingi za kigeni zimeathiri Kiswahili kwa viwango tofauti. Baadhi ya lugha hizi ni Kireno, Kiajemi, Kiarabu, Kihindi, Kijerumani, na Kiingereza. Hii inaonyesha wazi kwamba maendeleo katika sayansi na teknolojia yamekuwa na athari kubwa kwa lugha ya Kiswahili. Tafsiri ina jukumu katika kukuza na kueneza lugha, hasa kupitia mchakato wa kuhamisha miundo ya lugha kutoka lugha chanzi hadi lugha lengwa. Aidha, tafsiri huleta kuridhika kwa mtafsiri anapofanikiwa kukamilisha kazi yake kwa ufanisi (Mwansoko, 2016). Nassor (2017), kwa upande wake, anaeleza kwamba kiwango cha uundaji wa istilahi za Kiswahili kimeongezeka kwa kiasi kikubwa katika miaka ya hivi karibuni ikilinganishwa na miaka ya 1960. Anaongeza kuwa mwishoni mwa karne ya 19, jamii ya Waswahili ilipitia maendeleo makubwa katika sayansi na teknolojia, sambamba na nyanja nyingine. Kwa hivyo, lugha ya Kiswahili imepitia mabadiliko makubwa. Kwa hiyo, juhudi za kuendeleza Kiswahili kisarufi ziliongezeka ili kuendana na maendeleo haya. Pamoja na tafiti zinazochunguza maendeleo ya lugha ya Kiswahili kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia, makala hii pia inashughulikia suala hili lakini inajikita hasa kwenye uwanja wa upangaji istilahi katika maeneo ya baiolojia, fizikia na kemia. Adolph (2019), kwa upande wake, alichunguza istilahi katika nyanja za tiba na kompyuta, zinazotokana na Kiingereza katika Kiswahili na michakato ya uamilishaji wake. Matokeo ya utafiti wake yanaonyesha wazi kuwa Kiswahili kimepanua msamiati wake kupitia kuamilisha istilahi za tiba na kompyuta kutoka Kiingereza. Hivyo basi, uamilishaji huu umechochea ukuaji wa Kiswahili kutokana na upanuzi mkubwa wa msamiati wa kisayansi na kiteknolojia katika maeneo ya kompyuta na tiba. Mtaalamu huyu anaeleza kuwa mojawapo ya athari za uamilishaji ni kuongezeka kwa istilahi za Kiingereza ndani ya Kiswahili, na hivyo La hasha mbili. Mkakati wa Utafsiri wa Mikopo ya Istilahi za Kiingereza kuwa Kiswahili na Athari Zake: Uchambuzi wa Vitengo Vilivyochaguliwa kutoka katika Kamusi ya Baiolojia, Fizikia na Kemia ili kukidhi mahitaji ya mawasiliano miongoni mwa wanajamii. Lugha hukua na kubadilika kila siku kulingana na maendeleo ya jamii. Moja ya vigezo vikuu vya ukuaji na mabadiliko ya lugha ni kuongezeka kwa istilahi. Kwa mujibu wa Adolph (2019), ili istilahi ziweze kuongezeka katika lugha fulani, lazima istilahi mpya zianzishwe. Istilahi huundwa katika lugha ili utamaduni wake uweze kubeba dhana ambazo hapo awali hazikuwa sehemu ya utamaduni huo. Dokezo hili ni muhimu sana katika makala hii kwa kuwa linaonesha jinsi lugha inavyokua na kukidhi mahitaji ya mawasiliano kati ya wanajamii. Makala haya inachunguza mkakati wa utafsiri wa maneno ya Kiingereza kwa Kiswahili na athari zake kwa kuzingatia nyanja za biolojia, fizikia na kemia, tofauti na utafiti wa Adolph (2019), ambao unachunguza maendeleo ya lugha ya Kiswahili kupitia uhamasishaji wa istilahi za kitabibu na za kompyuta. Wasomi wengi ambao wamezungumzia ukopeshaji wanakubaliana kwamba ukopeshaji ni uhamishaji wa vipengele vya msamiati kutoka lugha moja kwenda nyingine (Haugen, 1950; Polomé, 1980; Adolph, 2014; Winford, 2003). Makala hii imegawanywa katika sehemu tano: Sehemu ya kwanza ni utangulizi, ambayo dhana kuu ya tafsiri na kazi zake zinaelezewa, pamoja na dhana ya tafsiri ya mkopo. Sehemu ya pili inaelezea nadharia iliyotumika kuongoza uchambuzi wa data katika makala hii. Sehemu ya tatu inaelezea mbinu. Sehemu ya nne inachambua data juu ya mkakati wa ukalimani wa mkopo kutoka Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili na athari zake. Majadiliano yanahusu istilahi katika nyanja za biolojia, fizikia, na kemia kutoka kwenye Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia, na Kemia (2012). Sehemu ya tano ni hitimisho. Nadharia  
Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi ilitumika kutoa data kwa makala hii. Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi inahusishwa na Kiingi (1989), ambaye ndiye mwanzilishi halisi wa nadharia hii. Baadaye, nadharia hii iliendelezwa zaidi na Kiingi (1992, 1998); Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001); Kevogo, Mukuthuria, na Ontieri (2018); na Kevogo (2020). Nadharia hii ina vigezo vya kisayansi kwa istilahi bora, ambavyo vina jukumu kuu katika tathmini iliyofanywa katika makala yetu. Wasomi kadhaa, kama vile Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008), wameeleza waziwazi kanuni mbalimbali ambazo zinapaswa kufuatwa wakati wa kukopa, kubadilisha, na kuunda istilahi kutoka lugha za asili na za kigeni hadi Kiswahili. Kanuni hizi zimefafanuliwa katika Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008). Hii inahusisha kuunda istilahi kwa kutumia Kiswahili, lugha za Kibantu, lugha nyingine za Kiafrika, na lugha za kigeni. Mbali na mitazamo mingine mingi iliyotolewa na Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (1997) kuhusiana na misingi hii, wanapendekeza miongozo ifuatayo: Istilahi zinapaswa kuakisi sifa bainifu za dhana zinazowakilisha (au angalau kupendekeza sifa hizo) na ziwe wazi kwa watumiaji lengwa. Ikiwa istilahi zitaundwa kwa kutumia mbinu za kuchanganya na kuunganisha maneno, vipengele vifuatavyo lazima vizingatiwe:
Idadi ya maneno yanayounganishwa au kuunganishwa haipaswi kuzidi mawili. Kistari hakipaswi kutumika kutenganisha istilahi ambatani, kwa sababu katika Kiswahili istilahi hizo kawaida hutamkwa kama neno moja, lenye mkazo mkuu kwenye silabi moja tu. Kwa mfano: -zao mtiririko (“flow products”) na -nusu kipenyo (“semi-diameter”). Istilahi kama hizo hazipaswi kuwa na zaidi ya silabi nne, kwa kuwa maneno ya Kiswahili kwa kawaida huwa na wastani wa silabi kati ya moja na tano. Istilahi lazima ziwe na uwezo mkubwa wa kutengeneza maneno yanayotokana ili kuzalisha istilahi nyingine zinazohusiana ndani ya uwanja husika au fani. Hii itaruhusu istilahi zinazowakilisha dhana zinazohusiana kwa karibu au zinazotokana na kila mmoja kuakisi uhusiano huo kwa mantiki. Kwa mfano: taifa (“nation”), taifisha (“nationalize”), utaifa (“nationalism”), -a kitaifa (“national”), -sio na taifa (“stateless”), na -siyo wa taifa (“un-national”). Istilahi (hasa zile zenye maana zinazokaribiana) lazima ziwe na mpangilio thabiti. Kwa mfano, istilahi zifuatazo zinaonyesha mpangilio unaokubalika: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, na kadhalika. Istilahi lazima ziwe sahihi, yaani ziakisi sifa za dhana zinazowakilisha (na si, kwa mfano, kupingana nazo). Kwa mfano, istilahi “tahakiki ya maandishi” si sahihi kwa sababu kwa ujumla inarejelea tathmini ya maandishi kwa ujumla, badala ya uchambuzi au uhakiki wa fasihi. Istilahi pia lazima ziwe fupi na kueleweka. Istilahi ndefu kama “majira ya majani kupukutika” (wakati wa msimu wa ukame unakaribia), hazifai kwa sababu hazifuati kanuni ya uchumi wa lugha. Kanuni hizi ni muhimu katika uundaji wa istilahi kwani zinaelekeza kuhusu nini kinapaswa kufanywa kuhusu utoaji wa maneno, uundaji, na urekebishaji. Zaidi ya hayo, mbinu za kuunda istilahi zimependekezwa. Hebu tuangalie mbinu hizi hapa chini: kwanza, tafsiri, hasa kutoka kwa lugha zinazojulikana kimataifa, kama Kiingereza, Kifaransa, Kihispania, na kadhalika. Pili, uundaji wa istilahi kulingana na mifumo ya dhana. Nadharia hii ni muhimu kwani inaweka misingi ya kufuatwa wakati wa mchakato wa tafsiri. Vivyo hivyo, inaelezea mbinu za uundaji wa istilahi.

Mbinu  
Kila mtafiti hutumia mbinu zinazofaa na wazi kwa utafiti wao. Makala hii ni matokeo ya utafiti wa maelezo uliofanywa maktabani na pia kwenye uwanja. Mtafiti alikusanya data kutoka Idara ya Lugha za Kigeni na Isimu, TATAKI kutoka Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam, pamoja na BAKIZA katika Wilaya ya Ubungo, Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, ambapo data ilikusanywa kwa kutumia mahojiano, dodoso, na chanzo cha data kutoka maktaba. Kulingana na Krishnaswami na Ranganatham (2005), mahojiano ni mbinu ya ukusanyaji data inayohusisha mazungumzo kati ya mtafiti na mhojiwa kwa lengo la kupata taarifa zinazohusiana na mada inayochunguzwa. Kwa kutumia mbinu ya mahojiano, mtafiti aliweza kufanya mahojiano ya ana kwa ana na wataalamu wa ukalimani kutoka idara na taasisi zilizotajwa hapo juu. Dodoso huandaliwa kwa lengo la kukusanya taarifa muhimu kutoka kwa wajibuji (Mugenda na Mugenda, 2003). Njia ya dodoso inaweza kufanywa ana kwa ana au kwa njia zisizo za ana kwa ana, kulingana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia. Maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia yamerahisisha uwasilishaji wa dodoso mbalimbali na watafiti kwa wajibuji wao kwa njia za kielektroniki (kupitia wavuti na barua pepe). Hata hivyo, mtafiti wa makala hii alitumia dodoso za ana kwa ana kwa sababu walengwa walikuwa katika eneo moja na walikuwa rahisi kufikiwa. Aidha, mtafiti alikagua maandiko mbalimbali kama vile majarida, tasnifu, kamusi, na kadhalika kutoka katika chanzo cha data cha maktaba. Matokeo ya utafiti

Tafsiri ya Mikopo katika Kemia  
Kama ilivyoelezwa hapo awali, mkakati wa tafsiri ya mikopo umetumika kote katika kutafsiri istilahi kutoka nyanja mbalimbali za Kiingereza kwenda Kiswahili. Kupitia matumizi ya mahojiano, dodoso, na chanzo cha maktaba, imebainika kuwa pamoja na Kiswahili kujipatia istilahi za sayansi ya baiolojia na ya kiumbo kupitia mkakati huu wa tafsiri ya mikopo, kimepitisha pia istilahi za kemia. Data iliyokusanywa inaangazia hali hii kwa mifano ifuatayo iliyoainishwa hapa chini:

Matokeo ya makala haya yanaonyesha kuwa istilahi katika biolojia, kemia, na fizikia imetafsiriwa kupitia mkakati wa ukopeshaji istilahi kutoka Kiingereza kwenda Kiswahili. Hii inatokana na mahitaji makubwa ya maneno haya miongoni mwa watumiaji wa Kiswahili, pamoja na maendeleo na ukuaji wa sayansi na teknolojia. Hali hii inalazimisha Kiswahili kutumia mkakati wa uhawilishaji istilahi ili kukidhi mahitaji ya mawasiliano ya wasemaji wa Kiswahili na kuingiza dhana zinazotokana na maneno haya. Madhara ya Uhawilishaji Istilahi Mkakati wa uhawilishaji istilahi umeleta athari mbalimbali kwa lugha tofauti duniani, hasa lugha ya Kiswahili. Kupitia mkakati wa uhawilishaji istilahi, kuna athari kadhaa zilizojitokeza katika lugha ya Kiswahili adhimu na hai pamoja na watumiaji wake kwa ujumla. Hebu tuchukue baadhi ya athari hizi: Jarida la Kiswahili na Lugha Nyingine za Kiafrika Juz. Hapana. Mkakati wa kutafsiri kwa kukopa istilahi za Kiingereza kwenda Kiswahili kwa kutumia mkopo wa istilahi kama njia ya kuunda istilahi za Kiswahili umecheza jukumu muhimu katika kutoa fursa kwa watafsiri wa lugha. Kwa mfano, TUKI (2012) imetafsiri msamiati wa kutosha unaohusiana na fani za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia kwa kutumia mkakati wa mkopo wa istilahi pamoja na aina nyingine za ukopaji; hata hivyo, makala hii inazingatia mkakati wa mkopo wa istilahi. Taasisi hii imetafsiri msamiati kutoka baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia kutoka Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili. Kweli, kazi hii imeleta utambulisho wa kimataifa kwa TUKI kutokana na umuhimu wake mkubwa katika fani za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia. Sambamba na utambuzi wa kimataifa, washiriki wa kazi hii pia wamenufaika kiuchumi kutokana na mauzo yaliyopatikana kupitia vitabu vilivyochapishwa, ikiwemo Kamusi ya Baiolojia, Fizikia, na Kemia iliyo sanifishwa. Hili linachangiwa na umuhimu wa yaliyomo, umakini katika maandalizi, na hasa ujuzi na utaalamu wa watunzi wa kamusi hiyo. Hii inaonyesha wazi kwamba watumiaji wake wana imani kubwa na kamusi hii na hivyo wako tayari kufanya manunuzi bila kusita. Kuenea kwa lugha ya Kiswahili duniani

Kutokana na taarifa kutoka kwa wahojaji (data za uwanja) pamoja na data za maktaba, mtafiti amebaini kwamba mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo uliotekelezwa na TUKI (2012) umechangia kutambulika kwa Kiswahili duniani kote, kwani nyanja za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia zinatumika kimataifa kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia, pamoja na umuhimu wake kwa wanafunzi wanaosoma masomo haya na kwa wasemaji wa Kiswahili kwa ujumla. Aidha, wasemaji wa lugha nyingine mbali na Kiswahili wanahitaji kujifunza msamiati wa fani hizi kwa lugha ya Kiswahili. Hali hii inawasababisha kununua vitabu mbalimbali vya Kiswahili, ikiwemo kamusi hii. Mambo haya yote yamechangia kwa kiasi kikubwa kuenea kwa Kiswahili duniani kote. Kuenea kwa Kiswahili duniani kumehamasisha watu kutoka nchi mbalimbali kujifunza Kiswahili, kukithamini, na kukipa umuhimu mkubwa.

Hitimisho

Uchambuzi katika makala hii unathibitisha hoja kuwa mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo umetumika kama mojawapo ya mbinu za kukopa istilahi za Kiingereza katika Kiswahili. Istilahi zilizochunguzwa katika makala hii ni zile zinazotoka katika fani za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia. Kwa upande wa baiolojia, istilahi kama vile: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, mimea ya mwaka miwili, nitrojeni, occiput, spermatid, na zoolojia zilibainishwa. Mtafiti pia alizingatia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo katika fani ya kemia. Zifuatazo ni baadhi ya istilahi zinazoshughulikiwa katika uwanja huu: kabisa, asetati, wingi tendaji, masi tendaji, asilishaji, nishati ya kiungo, dawa ya kuua wadudu, mionzi ya X, na ciencia ya vimeng’enya. Zaidi ya hayo, mtafiti wa makala hii pia amechunguza athari za mkakati wa uhawilishaji wa maneno katika lugha ya Kiswahili, watafsiri wa lugha, wanafunzi wa baiolojia, fizikia na kemia, wasemaji wa lugha nyingine wanaojifunza Kiswahili, na wasemaji wa Kiswahili kwa ujumla. Matokeo ya makala hii yameonyesha kuwa mkakati huu umekuwa na manufaa kwa watafsiri wa lugha, hasa wale wanaotafsiri kutoka Kiingereza kwenda Kiswahili. Mfano mzuri ni wataalamu wa TUKI ambao walitafsiri istilahi za nyanja hizi kutoka Kiingereza kwenda Kiswahili. Watafsiri hawa wameboresha hali zao za kiuchumi kutokana na uuzaji wa kamusi hii duniani kote. Pia imeonekana wazi kwamba TUKI, ambayo sasa inajulikana kama TATAKI, imetambuliwa na kuanzishwa duniani kote. Hii ni faida kwa taasisi kwani inapokea kazi. 1 Jina kamili la TUKI ni Taasisi ya Utafiti wa Kiswahili. Sasa inajulikana kama TATAKI, yaani, Taasisi ya Utafiti wa Kiswahili. Hapana. Asili mbalimbali, kwani kazi yao imesambaa duniani kote. Sambamba na hili, mkakati huu umechangia pia kuenea kwa Kiswahili duniani. Kazi hii na hii ni kivutio kwa wasemaji wa Kiswahili, wasemaji wa lugha nyingine wanaojifunza Kiswahili, na watu wengine. Mwandishi wa makala hii anapendekeza kwamba mbinu nyingine za kuazima kama vile uhalisishaji na urekebishaji zichunguzwe. Introduction  
Translation is the act of transferring a message contained in writing from the source language to the target language without altering the intended meaning in the source language. Thus, translation is regarded as a method of learning foreign languages, showcasing various cultures, and transmitting the knowledge and skills of other communities, such as information on scientific and technological advancements. The motivation that drives a person to translate the message from the source language to the target language is the desire to facilitate communication among speakers of different languages. We can therefore say that translation is a means or even a bridge to bring together various communities that speak different languages. Moreover, loan translation is one method of coining new vocabulary, where a concept from the source language is adopted and translated into the target language; for example, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, and so on. The strategy of borrowing through loan translation has gained momentum due to the significant developments occurring in the field of science and technology, coupled with society’s advancement into modernity, resulting in a high demand for vocabulary to describe various concepts. The researcher of this article investigates the loan translation strategy of English vocabulary into Kiswahili.

Tafsiri ni kitendo cha kuhamisha ujumbe uliomo katika maandishi kutoka lugha chanzi kwenda lugha lengwa bila kubadili maana iliyokusudiwa katika lugha chanzi. Hivyo basi, tafsiri huchukuliwa kama mbinu ya kujifunza lugha za kigeni, kuonyesha tamaduni mbalimbali, na kuhamisha maarifa na stadi za jamii nyingine, kama vile taarifa kuhusu maendeleo ya kisayansi na kiteknolojia. Msukumo unaomfanya mtu kutafsiri ujumbe kutoka lugha chanzi kwenda lugha lengwa ni hamu ya kufanikisha mawasiliano kati ya wazungumzaji wa lugha tofauti. Kwa hiyo, tunaweza kusema kuwa tafsiri ni njia au hata daraja la kuunganisha jamii mbalimbali zinazozungumza lugha tofauti. Aidha, tafsiri ya mkopo ni mbinu mojawapo ya kuunda msamiati mpya, ambapo dhana kutoka lugha chanzi inachukuliwa na kutafsiriwa katika lugha lengwa; kwa mfano, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, na kadhalika. Mkakati wa kukopa kupitia tafsiri ya mkopo umeongezeka kasi kutokana na maendeleo makubwa yanayotokea katika uwanja wa sayansi na teknolojia, pamoja na maendeleo ya jamii kuingia katika ukisasa, na hivyo kusababisha kuhitajika kwa msamiati mwingi wa kuelezea dhana mbalimbali. discourses.translated_txt: Wasomi kadhaa, kama vile Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008), wameeleza waziwazi kanuni mbalimbali ambazo zinapaswa kufuatwa wakati wa kukopa, kubadilisha, na kuunda istilahi kutoka lugha za asili na za kigeni hadi Kiswahili. Kanuni hizi zimefafanuliwa katika Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008).

discourses.source_txt:
This involves creating terminology using Swahili, Bantu languages, other African languages, and foreign languages. In addition to many other views expressed by Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (1997) regarding these principles, they recommend the following guidelines: Terminology should reflect the distinctive features of the concepts they represent (or at least suggest such features) and be clear to the intended users. If terminology is formed using compounding and word combination techniques, the following aspects must be considered:
The number of words combined or joined should not exceed two. Hyphens should not be used to separate compound terms, because in Swahili such terms are usually pronounced as a single word, with the primary stress on only one syllable. For example: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") and -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Such terms should not have more than four syllables, since Swahili words usually have an average of between one and five syllables. Terminology must be highly derivable in order to generate other related terms within the relevant domain or field. This will allow terms representing closely related or derivationally connected concepts to logically reflect that connection. For example: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), and -siyo wa taifa ("un-national").
discourses.translated_txt:
Hii inahusisha kuunda istilahi kwa kutumia Kiswahili, lugha za Kibantu, lugha nyingine za Kiafrika, na lugha za kigeni. Mbali na mitazamo mingine mingi iliyotolewa na Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (1997) kuhusiana na misingi hii, wanapendekeza miongozo ifuatayo: Istilahi zinapaswa kuakisi sifa bainifu za dhana zinazowakilisha (au angalau kupendekeza sifa hizo) na ziwe wazi kwa watumiaji lengwa. Ikiwa istilahi zitaundwa kwa kutumia mbinu za kuchanganya na kuunganisha maneno, vipengele vifuatavyo lazima vizingatiwe:
Idadi ya maneno yanayounganishwa au kuunganishwa haipaswi kuzidi mawili. Kistari hakipaswi kutumika kutenganisha istilahi ambatani, kwa sababu katika Kiswahili istilahi hizo kawaida hutamkwa kama neno moja, lenye mkazo mkuu kwenye silabi moja tu. Kwa mfano: -zao mtiririko (“flow products”) na -nusu kipenyo (“semi-diameter”). Istilahi kama hizo hazipaswi kuwa na zaidi ya silabi nne, kwa kuwa maneno ya Kiswahili kwa kawaida huwa na wastani wa silabi kati ya moja na tano. Istilahi lazima ziwe na uwezo mkubwa wa kutengeneza maneno yanayotokana ili kuzalisha istilahi nyingine zinazohusiana ndani ya uwanja husika au fani. Hii itaruhusu istilahi zinazowakilisha dhana zinazohusiana kwa karibu au zinazotokana na kila mmoja kuakisi uhusiano huo kwa mantiki. Kwa mfano: taifa (“nation”), taifisha (“nationalize”), utaifa (“nationalism”), -a kitaifa (“national”), -sio na taifa (“stateless”), na -siyo wa taifa (“un-national”).

discourses.source_txt: Terminology (especially those with overlapping shades of meaning) must maintain consistency in sequence. The following terms, for example, demonstrate an acceptable alignment of sequence: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, and so on. Terminology must be adequate, meaning it should reflect the characteristics of the concepts they represent (and not, for instance, contradict them). For example, the term “tahakiki ya maandishi” is inappropriate because it generally refers to the evaluation of writing at large, rather than the analysis or critique of literature. Terminology must also be short and understandable. Lengthy terms, such as “majira ya majani kupukutika” (when the dry season approaches), are unsuitable because they do not adhere to the principle of linguistic economy.

Research Findings

The findings of this article were obtained after an investigation and analysis of data concerning the development of Swahili through the loan translation of terminology from English. Loan translation is a strategy for term creation involving word-for-word transfer of both structural elements and general concepts. The structure of terms created using the loan translation strategy changes to conform to the morphological and phonological rules of the target language. From the methods of interviews, questionnaires, and the library data source, it was found that several terms in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry—through the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012)—have been incorporated into Swahili from English via the loan translation strategy.

Benefits for Language Translators and Global Recognition of TUKI

The strategy of borrowing English terms into Swahili through loan translation as a method for creating Swahili terminology has played a significant role in providing opportunities for language translators. For instance, TUKI (2012) has translated an adequate vocabulary related to the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry by employing the loan translation strategy and other forms of borrowing; however, this article focuses on the loan translation strategy. This institution has translated vocabulary from biology, physics, and chemistry from English into Swahili. Indeed, this work has brought global recognition to TUKI due to its great importance in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. Alongside international recognition, those involved in this work have also benefited economically from sales made through published books, including the standardized Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary. This is attributed to the significance of its contents, the care taken in its preparation, and especially the expertise and professionalism of the dictionary’s compilers.

Kwa mfano, TUKI (2012) imetafsiri msamiati wa kutosha unaohusiana na fani za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia kwa kutumia mkakati wa mkopo wa istilahi pamoja na aina nyingine za ukopaji; hata hivyo, makala hii inazingatia mkakati wa mkopo wa istilahi. The Global Spread of the Swahili Language

Based on information from respondents (field data) as well as library data, the researcher has found that the loan translation strategy implemented by TUKI (2012) has contributed to the worldwide recognition of Swahili, since the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry are used globally due to advancements in science and technology, as well as their importance to students studying these subjects and to Swahili speakers in general. Furthermore, speakers of other languages apart from Swahili need to learn the vocabulary of these fields in the Swahili language. This situation leads them to acquire several Swahili language books, including this dictionary. All these factors have significantly contributed to the overall spread of Swahili throughout the world. The global spread of Swahili has encouraged people from various countries to learn Swahili, appreciate it, and value it highly.

Conclusion

The analysis in this article confirms the argument that the loan translation strategy has been used as one of the methods for borrowing English terminology into Swahili. The terms examined in this article are those from the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. In the case of biology, terms such as: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, biennial plants, nitrogen, occiput, spermatid, and zoology were identified. The researcher also considered the loan translation strategy in the field of chemistry.

Kuenea kwa Kiswahili duniani kumehamasisha watu kutoka nchi mbalimbali kujifunza Kiswahili, kukithamini, na kukipa umuhimu mkubwa.

Hitimisho

Uchambuzi katika makala hii unathibitisha hoja kuwa mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo umetumika kama mojawapo ya mbinu za kukopa istilahi za Kiingereza katika Kiswahili. Istilahi zilizochunguzwa katika makala hii ni zile zinazotoka katika fani za baiolojia, fizikia, na kemia. Kwa upande wa baiolojia, istilahi kama vile: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, mimea ya mwaka miwili, nitrojeni, occiput, spermatid, na zoolojia zilibainishwa. Mtafiti pia alizingatia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo katika fani ya kemia.
